newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent, other grades firmer as Europe shivers.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent, other grades firmer as Europe shivers.

text.p: Dated Brent and other North Sea crudes firmed on Monday, supported by improving refinery margins as gas oil demand got a seasonal boost from icy weather across much of Europe, traders said.

A Brent cargo due to load Jan 11-13 was sold for Feb Brent +15 cents -- five cents more expensive than on Friday -- to a Swiss-based trader but some dealers valued the benchmark grade a couple of cents cheaper.
"There was a Jan 9-11 cargo on offer today at Feb plus 12 cents and it was shown to that buyer," said a trader.
Feb Brent gained 37 cents to $23.79 a barrel by 1820 GMT.

Dated Brent was also supported by news that system operator Shell UK had cancelled its own equity cargo due to load Jan 15-17, trimming the January tally to 43 standard cargoes plus 1.509 million barrels in top-ups.

Earlier, a Brent cargo nominated loading dates of Jan 14-16 on Monday was kept by equity holder Esso, while a second, brought forward a day to the Jan 14-16 loading period by equity holder Elf, was "clocked" to U.S.-based trader Cargill, traders said.
Brent paper spread talk was thin but CFDs were active, the Dec 6-10 dates trading at a firmer Feb Brent +10 cents.
Differentials for other North Sea grades also looked to be moving higher with a million barrels of Jan 15-18 Oseberg trading at Dated Brent +43 cents, slightly firmer than pre-Christmas levels.
In the Mediterranean spot markets were extremely thin, traders said. The crude pipeline feeding Russia's Novorossiisk port on the Black Sea was shut because storage tanks were full.
Syrian price talks for January crude continued with lifters still hoping state-owned Sytrol would improve on its latest offer of Dated Brent -25 cents a barrel.
